culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Milan Cathedral (Duomo): decent dress is required. No sleeveless or low-cut tops, shorts, miniskirts or hats inside the cathedral. Wear comfortable shoes for the terraces.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: The Duomo is a working cathedral; its regulation (July 2025) sets conduct and access rules.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Veneranda Fabbrica del Duomo di Milano
culture-and-protocol.note: Site-level rules from the site's own authority.

laws.rule: Since 1 January 2025, Milan bans smoking tobacco in all outdoor public places, streets included, except isolated spots where you can stay at least 10 m from other people (Air Quality Regulation, article 9). E-cigarettes are not covered.
laws.heading: Comune di Milano, Regolamento per la qualità dell'aria (delibera 56/2020)

laws.rule: In Lombardy mushroom collection is generally free, but mountain communities and eligible park authorities may require a locally valid paid permit. Check the rules with the authority for the actual collection area before collecting.
laws.heading: Lombardia: raccolta funghi, le regole

laws.rule: Como charges an imposta di soggiorno (tourist tax) per person per night, for up to 4 consecutive nights, from 1 January 2024 (Giunta resolution 387 of 10 November 2023). Hotels EUR 5 (4 and 5 star), EUR 4 (3 star), EUR 3 (1 and 2 star); tourist-hotel residences EUR 5 (4 star), EUR 4 (3), EUR 3 (2); holiday flats, rooms and B&Bs EUR 3; hostels, alpine huts, campsites, holiday villages and agritourism EUR 2. That is about A$3.18 to A$7.95 (A$1 = EUR 0.6293, RBA 30 October 2026). This is the city's table as read; whether a newer one exists was not checked.
laws.penalty_signal: EUR 2 to EUR 5 per person per night (about A$3.18 to A$7.95)
laws.heading: Comune di Como, Tariffe dell'imposta di soggiorno (GC 387/2023)

laws.rule: Bergamo's imposta di soggiorno (tourist tax; regulation of 12 December 2011, council resolution 213) is worked out as 7% of the nightly cost of the stay per person, before VAT and extras, capped at EUR 5 per person per night (about A$7.95 (A$1 = EUR 0.6293, RBA 30 October 2026)), for up to 5 consecutive nights. Non-residents pay it to the host. The city page also carries older wording that gives 6% for some lodging types, so 7% is the figure on the payment page read.
laws.penalty_signal: up to EUR 5 per person per night (about A$7.95)
laws.heading: Comune di Bergamo, Versare l'imposta di soggiorno (IDS)
